summary: The statistical core correctly treats specimens as replicates, suppresses inference below three specimens per group, reports effect sizes and confidence intervals, and separates raw count, sampled-area density, and sampled-volume density. However, acceptance is blocked by two reporting-path defects: the production workflow rejects studies with multiple comparison groups even though the report generator and design contract support them, and the cited RC6 PDF/spreadsheet consistency receipt validates an older report metric contract rather than the concise reporting contract at the reviewed commit.

findings.title: Production study workflow rejects the supported multigroup design
findings.impact: A study with one reference and two or more comparison groups cannot generate biological reports through the production workflow. Consequently, not every declared comparison is reported and the across-comparison multiplicity correction is unreachable from the actual GUI/study execution path.

findings.recommendation: Change the production workflow to resolve one reference plus all manifest-declared comparison groups and pass every comparison to the generator. Add an end-to-end focused test through generate_study_between_sample_analysis using one reference and at least two comparison groups, asserting per-contrast packages and the combined cross-contrast q-value table.

findings.title: Primary count wording can overstate what the sampled ROI establishes
findings.impact: The question text asks how many nuclei are present in each specimen, while the implementation counts reconstructed technical-valid nuclei within the acquired ROI and incomplete Z coverage. Although adjacent caveats mitigate this, isolated reuse of the question can be interpreted as whole-specimen abundance.

findings.recommendation: Use 'within the sampled ROI/acquisition' in the count question and display label wherever it travels, while retaining the separate raw count, sampled-area density, sampled-volume density, and coverage diagnostics.
